37992593.model_family: Gaussian Mixture Model subtyping; amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) analysis
37992593.clinical_problem: subtyping depression to guide targeted repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS)
37992593.patient_population: 238 major depressive disorder patients and 66 healthy controls at Center 1 (subtyping); 72 hospitalized depressed youths at Center 2 (treatment application)
37992593.model_description: Resting-state fMRI amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) maps are input to a Gaussian Mixture Model that clusters depressed patients into two neuroimaging subtypes (archetypal and atypical); subtype membership then selects an rTMS target region (dorsomedial prefrontal cortex or occipital cortex) applied to hospitalized depressed youths.
37992593.dataset_size: 238 MDD patients and 66 healthy controls (Center 1); 72 hospitalized depressed youths (Center 2)
37992593.headline_result: symptom response 90.00% in archetypal depression and 70.73% in atypical depression after subtype-targeted rTMS
37992593.study_design: two-stage multicenter development and clinical application study

38666133.model_family: support vector machine on graph-based morphological network features
38666133.clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls using structural brain network topology
38666133.patient_population: 25 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with MDD and 19 healthy controls
38666133.model_description: T1-weighted MRI is used to build single-subject morphological brain networks (based on cortical thickness, fractal dimension, gyrification index, sulcus depth); graph-based topological features from the cortical-thickness network are fed into a support vector machine that outputs a binary MDD-vs-healthy-control classification.
38666133.headline_result: 87.6% accuracy distinguishing adolescent MDD from healthy controls using cortical-thickness network topology
38666133.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

35964072.model_family: deep transfer learning (13 CNN architectures, best DarkNet53)
35964072.clinical_problem: detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) on pelvic X-ray
35964072.patient_population: 354 subjects (120 DDH, 234 normal) from two hospitals in northern Jordan
35964072.model_description: Pelvic anteroposterior X-ray images are classified as DDH or normal by thirteen deep transfer-learning CNN models, without requiring explicit angle measurements; the best-performing model (DarkNet53) is reported.
35964072.headline_result: DarkNet53: 96.3% accuracy, F1 95%, precision 90.6%, recall 100%, specificity 94.3%

33041749.clinical_problem: early prediction of cognitive deficit at 2 years of age in very preterm infants
33041749.patient_population: 110 very preterm infants (≤32 weeks gestational age)
33041749.model_description: Brain structural connectome, derived from diffusion tensor imaging at term-equivalent age and represented as a 2D image, is input to a transfer-learning-enhanced CNN that outputs a cognitive-deficit classification and a continuous cognitive score, predicting Bayley-III cognitive assessment at 2 years of corrected age.

25687738.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric unipolar depression from healthy controls using brain structure
25687738.patient_population: 25 pediatric unipolar depression patients and 26 demographically matched healthy controls
25687738.model_description: T1-weighted structural MRI is used to derive multiple neuromorphometric indices (cortical thickness, volume, cortical folding); a support vector machine trained on these indices classifies individual subjects as having pediatric unipolar depression or being a healthy control.
25687738.dataset_size: 25 pediatric unipolar depression patients, 26 healthy controls
25687738.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

25485393.model_family: stacked auto-encoder (deep learning) with sparse patch matching
25485393.clinical_problem: segmenting the hippocampus on infant brain MRI to study early brain development
25485393.model_description: T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI are input to a Stacked Auto Encoder that learns deep feature representations combining both contrasts; these learned features drive a sparse patch-matching method that transfers hippocampus labels from multiple atlases onto a new infant image, producing a hippocampus segmentation.

20681014.exclusion_reason: adult word-learning fMRI study, no pediatric population

35396036.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for suspected congenital heart disease
35396036.model_description: Narrative review describing how AI algorithms applied to fetal echocardiography could improve image acquisition, image optimization, automated measurements, outlier identification, diagnostic classification, and outcome prediction for congenital heart disease; no single model is developed.

32714147.exclusion_reason: animal (mouse) model study, not human imaging

31521335.exclusion_reason: adult/young-adult alcohol relapse fMRI study, not pediatric

23922750.body_region: fetal brain (frontal lobe, basal ganglia, mesencephalon, cerebellum)
23922750.clinical_problem: predicting abnormal neonatal neurobehavior in small-for-gestational-age fetuses from fetal brain MRI texture
23922750.patient_population: 91 small-for-gestational-age fetuses at 37 weeks gestational age
23922750.model_description: Quantitative texture features are extracted from fetal MRI of the frontal lobe, basal ganglia, mesencephalon and cerebellum; machine learning models these textural features to predict abnormal neonatal neurobehavior (NBAS test) after birth.
23922750.headline_result: prediction accuracy 95.12% frontal lobe, 95.56% basal ganglia, 93.18% mesencephalon, 83.33% cerebellum

24095098.clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve types and predicting surgical fusion levels
24095098.patient_population: 1,776 patients surgically treated for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
24095098.model_description: Cobb angles and curve geometry measured on spine radiographs are input to a Kohonen self-organizing map (a type of artificial neural network) that clusters patients into curve-type nodes; the map's clustering is compared with the Lenke classification and surgeons' actual fusion-level choices.
24095098.headline_result: topographic error 0.02; Lenke classification predicted fused regions in 46% of individual cases vs. 82% of SOM nodes
24095098.study_design: retrospective multicenter analysis with technical concept development

22307098.exclusion_reason: computerized lung sound (auscultation) analysis, non-radiologic imaging

22959658.model_description: Brain MRI is segmented into internal and external caudate nucleus structures using a machine-learning-based automatic segmentation method; new volume-relation features (3D Dissociated Dipoles) are then used to classify subjects for ADHD diagnostic assistance.
22959658.study_design: retrospective single-center method development and evaluation

37163546.model_family: support vector machine on structural and functional MRI features
37163546.clinical_problem: identifying brain structural and functional abnormalities to distinguish young children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children
37163546.patient_population: 67 children with ASD (aged 2-7 years) and 39 age-matched typically developing controls
37163546.model_description: Structural (voxel-based morphometry) and resting-state functional MRI features are combined and input to a support vector machine that classifies children as having autism spectrum disorder or being typically developing.

37163546.headline_result: 86.2% accuracy discriminating ASD from typically developing children using combined structural and functional features
37163546.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

37666981.clinical_problem: automatic measurement of the Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
37666981.patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full-spine standing X-ray
37666981.model_description: A convolutional neural network automatically detects vertebrae on full-length spine X-rays and measures the Cobb angle; its output is compared with manual measurements from six physicians.
37666981.headline_result: ICC 0.973 for major curve vs. six physicians; AI measured 1.7-2.2° smaller than physicians

34346086.model_family: resting-state dynamic causal modeling-based support vector machine (rs-DCM-SVM)
34346086.clinical_problem: diagnosing drug-naive Rolandic epilepsy from resting-state brain network imbalance
34346086.patient_population: discovery cohort: 76 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 76 normal controls; replication cohort: 59 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 60 normal controls

34346086.study_design: multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with discovery and replication cohorts

32607611.model_family: principal component analysis + support vector machine
32607611.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric mild traumatic brain injury from typically developing controls when conventional imaging is normal
32607611.patient_population: 24 adolescents (14 with mild TBI, 10 typically developing controls), aged 10-16 years
32607611.model_description: Diffusion MRI fiber tractography is used to compute edge density imaging maps of brain connectivity; PCA and an SVM classifier applied to these maps distinguish mild TBI from typically developing controls, compared against neurocognitive tests and conventional fractional anisotropy.
32607611.headline_result: sensitivity 79%, specificity 100%, AUC 94% for edge density imaging + SVM-PCA
32607611.study_design: prospective single-center proof-of-concept diagnostic accuracy study

23299250.exclusion_reason: computational cognitive model of category learning, not applied to radiologic images

19418048.patient_population: 24 children (age 3-18 years) with known primary tumors and lung nodules
19418048.model_description: Chest CT scans are analyzed by a commercially available computer-aided detection system that flags candidate pulmonary nodules; CAD sensitivity is compared against four radiologists, stratified by nodule size and location.
19418048.headline_result: CAD sensitivity 34% overall (80% for nodules ≥4mm) vs. radiologist sensitivity 68-79%; 0.9 CAD false positives per study

38165551.model_family: 3D residual neural network (multimodal, fusing low-dose CT)
38165551.clinical_problem: reducing pediatric total-body PET/CT scan time (and sedation need) while preserving image quality
38165551.patient_population: 270 pediatric patients undergoing total-body 18F-FDG PET/CT (uEXPLORER scanner)
38165551.model_description: Short-duration PET list-mode data (6-150 s) and low-dose CT images are fused as input to a 3D residual convolutional neural network that outputs a full-length, high-dose-quality PET image, aiming to shorten scan time without sedation-related motion artifacts.
38165551.headline_result: 60-second multimodal AI reconstruction produced PET image quality comparable to the full 600-second acquisition
38165551.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and evaluation

38319162.model_description: Narrative review of strategies to reduce gadolinium-based contrast agent exposure in glioma and meningioma MRI, including reduced/omitted contrast protocols and artificial-intelligence methods that generate synthetic postcontrast images from non-contrast or low-dose scans; no single model is developed.

38355987.exclusion_reason: adult total-body PET/CT study, pediatric only mentioned as future application

38585353.clinical_problem: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field brain MRI in young people
38585353.model_description: T1- and T2-weighted images from a 64mT low-field portable MRI system are processed by SynthSR, a convolutional-neural-network super-resolution method, to produce images with improved correspondence to matched 3T high-field images; performance is compared against a multi-orientation averaging alternative.
38585353.headline_result: SynthSR improved correspondence to high-field images to r=0.85-0.97 for most brain volume measures (vs. r=0.60-0.88 uncorrected); cortical thickness correspondence remained poor (r=0.14)

38809123.clinical_problem: applying AI to pediatric cancer imaging acquisition, processing, diagnosis, staging and treatment-response monitoring
38809123.patient_population: children with cancer undergoing diagnostic imaging
38809123.model_description: Narrative review of current AI applications in pediatric cancer imaging, covering image acquisition, processing, reconstruction, segmentation, diagnosis, staging, and treatment-response monitoring, and the challenges (data scarcity, anatomic diversity, nonstandardized protocols) limiting clinical translation; no single model is developed.

37241224.exclusion_reason: systematic review explicitly excludes pediatric studies

37324652.clinical_problem: using machine learning to assess fetal well-being and predict/diagnose obstetric disease (gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, fetal anomalies)
37324652.model_description: Narrative review of machine-learning tools for obstetric disease prediction and diagnosis, including automated diagnostic imaging of fetal anomalies and assessment of fetoplacental and cervix function using ultrasound and MRI; no single model is developed.

37467869.model_family: adult-trained deep learning algorithm applied to pediatric images
37467869.clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs using an adult-trained AI algorithm
37467869.patient_population: pediatric patients aged 1 to 5 years (publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset)
37467869.model_description: A publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset is analyzed using an AI pneumonia-detection algorithm from TorchXRayVision that was trained on adult images; a 60% threshold produces a binary pneumonia prediction, compared against dataset labels, to test whether adult-trained algorithms generalize to pediatric patients.
37467869.headline_result: sensitivity 79.83%, specificity 67.66%, accuracy 76.54%, F1 0.83 overall; PPV fell to 69.9% and F1 to 0.74 for viral pneumonia
37467869.study_design: retrospective external validation of an adult-trained algorithm on a pediatric dataset

37536046.model_description: Gray-matter volumes (AAL3 atlas) and cortical-thickness features (Destrieux atlas), combined with personal characteristic data, are input to several classifiers (KNN, logistic regression, linear and RBF SVM, random forest) that output an ADHD-vs-typically-developing classification.

35125417.model_description: Infant hip ultrasound sweeps and single 2D images are read by an FDA-cleared commercial AI software package (Medo Hip), which measures the alpha angle and classifies DDH status; its agreement is compared against 12 human readers of varying experience (radiologists, sonographers, clinicians, DDH subspecialists).

35144197.model_family: spatio-temporal directed acyclic graph deep learning with attention
35144197.clinical_problem: predicting cognition and age from resting-state functional brain network data
35144197.patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort (n=7,693, children) and OASIS-3 cohort (n=1,786, older adults)
35144197.model_description: Resting-state fMRI time series and derived functional connectivity are input to a deep-learning framework combining a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network with a functional-connectivity convolutional network and an attention mechanism, which outputs predicted cognition scores or brain age.

35144197.study_design: retrospective multicenter method development and validation study

35348867.clinical_problem: automatically evaluating and diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis on full-spine X-ray
35348867.patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full spinal anteroposterior X-ray
35348867.model_description: Full-spine anteroposterior X-rays are analyzed by a deep learning ensemble network that automatically measures the Cobb angle, apical vertebrae, and upper/lower vertebrae, and assesses anatomical balance parameters, validated against a public dataset and an external hospital.
35348867.dataset_size: 788 training + 185 internal test images; external validation set from a separate hospital; also validated on a public dataset
35348867.headline_result: Cobb angle accuracy/recall 89.36%/97.35%; mean absolute error 1.07° for Cobb angle; measurement 200x faster than radiologists
35348867.study_design: retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with external validation

35667473.clinical_problem: classifying pediatric posterior fossa brain tumor type (medulloblastoma vs. ependymoma vs. astrocytoma)

35667473.model_description: Whole-tumor radiomic features are extracted from manually segmented MRI (including ADC sequence) and the top ten features selected by a forest-based method are input to a random forest classifier that outputs the histologic tumor type.
35667473.headline_result: validation accuracy 0.938; sensitivity 1.000/0.948/0.808 and specificity 0.952/0.926/1.000 for EP/MB/PA respectively

35741233.clinical_problem: automating Graf standard plane detection and angle measurement for infant hip ultrasound (DDH diagnosis)
35741233.patient_population: infants undergoing hip ultrasound for suspected developmental dysplasia of the hip
35741233.model_description: Hip ultrasound images or video are processed by a three-module deep-learning framework (anatomical-structure detection, standard-plane scoring, angle measurement) that automatically identifies the Graf standard plane and measures alpha/beta angles to classify Graf type I/II hips, in both static-image and dynamic-video modes.
35741233.headline_result: static mode: mean absolute error α 1.71°, β 2.40°, classification accuracy 94.71%; dynamic mode: accuracy 89.51% at 31 fps
35741233.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

35942441.model_family: boundary-aware grid contextual attention convolutional network
35942441.clinical_problem: segmenting osteosarcoma tumor boundaries on MRI
35942441.model_description: Osteosarcoma MRI images are segmented by a novel network (BA-GCA Net) that combines grid contextual attention, a statistical texture learning block, and a spatial transformer block to better capture tumor texture and boundary despite vague or irregular tumor margins.

35942441.headline_result: higher segmentation accuracy than existing methods (no single summary metric given), with only a slight increase in parameters/computation
35942441.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development study with ablation experiments

36092792.clinical_problem: measuring the angle of progression to assess fetal head descent during labor
36092792.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing transperineal ultrasound during labor
36092792.model_description: Transperineal ultrasound images are processed by a multitask network with a shared encoder and three task-specific decoders that recognize the standard imaging plane, segment the pubic symphysis and fetal head, and detect pubic-symphysis endpoints, from which the angle of progression is automatically computed.
36092792.headline_result: standard-plane classification accuracy 92.26%; mean AoP error 3.898° (STD 3.192°); Pearson r=0.964 vs. manual measurement
36092792.study_design: retrospective technical development and agreement study

36140628.model_family: ensemble of eight fine-tuned segmentation architectures (UNet, UNet++, Attention UNet, UNet3+, TransUNet, FPN, LinkNet, Deeplabv3) with EfficientNetB0 backbone
36140628.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal head on ultrasound and estimating gestational age and fetal weight

36481929.model_description: Gray-matter regional brain volumes and psychometric scores collected at age 14 are input to a voting classifier (random forest, SVM, logistic regression) that predicts prospective clinical anxiety onset 4-8 years later; Shapley values identify the most contributory features.
36481929.headline_result: AUC 0.68 for prospective prediction of pooled anxiety disorders

36759257.model_description: Systematic review and primer on predictive modeling methods applied to fetal, infant and toddler (FIT) neuroimaging, summarizing topics, modalities and methods used across more than 100 studies from the past decade and outlining ethical and methodological considerations; no single model is developed.

33548168.model_description: Ultrasound images of fetal faces are labeled into seven expression categories (eye blinking, mouthing, no expression, scowling, smiling, tongue expulsion, yawning); a deep-learning AI classifier trained on these images outputs a facial-expression category and confidence score.
33548168.dataset_size: images from fetuses across five retained expression categories (e.g. 147 mouthing images, 320 no-expression images)

33992626.patient_population: 64 children and young adults (aged 1-23 years) treated with proton therapy
33992626.model_description: Pretreatment abdominal/pelvic cone-beam CT images, with body width normalized to reduce size-variation effects, are input to a cycle-consistent generative adversarial network that outputs corrected CT-equivalent images for proton dose recalculation, compared against same-day repeat planning CT.

34648114.clinical_problem: identifying pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs and testing generalizability to an external population

34707474.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.125 weeks internally; 0.508 weeks on external validation

33102411.headline_result: significant correlation predicting language outcome (r=0.48-0.76) and motor outcome (r=0.53-0.57), p<0.05

33240068.model_family: convolutional neural network (transfer learning) with support vector machine
33240068.clinical_problem: identifying epilepsy from hippocampal diffusion kurtosis imaging when MRI is otherwise negative
33240068.patient_population: 59 children with hippocampal epilepsy and 70 age- and sex-matched normal controls
33240068.model_description: Diffusion kurtosis imaging parameter maps (FA, MD, MK) of the segmented hippocampus are input to a transfer-learning CNN for feature extraction, followed by a support vector machine that classifies subjects as epilepsy patients or normal controls.
33240068.headline_result: classifier accuracy 90.8% for patients vs. normal controls
33240068.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

30642755.clinical_problem: identifying epileptogenic lesions (focal cortical dysplasia) in children with intractable epilepsy, including MRI-negative cases
30642755.patient_population: pediatric cohort with medically intractable epilepsy, MRI-positive and MRI-negative for focal cortical dysplasia
30642755.model_description: T1-weighted, T2-weighted and FLAIR MRI sequences are processed with morphometric and gray-level co-occurrence texture features, which are input to a 2-step Bayesian classifier that flags candidate epileptogenic lesions, evaluated separately in MRI-positive and MRI-negative epilepsy cases.
30642755.headline_result: combining all three sequences: 97% subjectwise sensitivity in MRI-positive cases and 70% in MRI-negative cases; 100% healthy-subject rejection

31077983.model_family: previously trained machine learning classifier (resting-state fMRI network localization)
31077983.clinical_problem: localizing sensorimotor brain function noninvasively before epilepsy surgery, as an alternative to invasive stimulation mapping
31077983.patient_population: 16 pediatric patients aged 3.1-18.6 years with medically refractory epilepsy undergoing invasive electrographic monitoring
31077983.model_description: Resting-state fMRI data from pediatric epilepsy patients are analyzed by a machine learning classifier (previously trained and validated in adults) that localizes sensorimotor resting-state networks; results are compared with direct electrocortical stimulation mapping, the clinical gold standard.
31077983.headline_result: comparable functional localization between resting-state fMRI classifier and electrocortical stimulation mapping (no single summary statistic given)
31077983.study_design: prospective single-center comparative diagnostic accuracy study

31115936.clinical_problem: correcting off-resonance artifacts to enable faster pediatric body MR angiography
31115936.model_description: Short-readout (long scan-time, low-artifact) MRA scans are used as reference and augmented with simulated off-resonance to train a residual CNN (Off-ResNet); applied to faster long-readout 3D-cones scans, the network corrects off-resonance blurring, compared against an autofocus method and radiologist scoring of anatomical features.
31115936.headline_result: long-readout scans corrected with Off-ResNet were noninferior to short-readout reference scans on radiologist scoring (P<.05); superior RMSE/SSIM/PSNR vs. autofocus (P<.01), with 59.3% shorter scan time
31115936.study_design: prospective single-center technical development and reader-validation study

31737980.clinical_problem: identifying children and adolescents with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder from regional brain volumes
31737980.patient_population: training: 79 FASD (5.7-18.9y) and 81 controls (5.8-18.5y); testing: 67 FASD (6.0-19.6y) and 74 controls (5.2-19.5y), from two independent datasets
31737980.model_description: 87 regional brain volumes extracted from 3D T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer are input to a support vector machine that classifies children/adolescents as having fetal alcohol spectrum disorder or being a healthy control; separate models are also built by sex.
31737980.dataset_size: training: 79 FASD + 81 controls; testing: 67 FASD + 74 controls (independent dataset)
31737980.study_design: retrospective multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with independent test dataset

28364401.exclusion_reason: fMRI group-comparison study in NF1, no AI/ML component

29255892.clinical_problem: predicting the need for postnatal cerebrospinal fluid diversion (hydrocephalus treatment) in fetal ventriculomegaly
29255892.patient_population: discovery cohort: 25 patients requiring postnatal CSF diversion matched with 25 who did not, from 253 fetal ventriculomegaly patients; replication cohort: 24 patients from a separate institution
29255892.model_description: Linear measurements, area, volume and morphologic features are extracted from fetal MRI; a machine learning algorithm integrates these multiple features to predict which fetuses with ventriculomegaly will require postnatal CSF diversion, validated in an independent replication cohort.
29255892.dataset_size: discovery cohort 25+25 matched patients (from 253-patient database); replication cohort 24 patients
29255892.headline_result: discovery cohort: 82% accuracy, 80% sensitivity, 84% specificity; replication cohort: 91% accuracy, 75% sensitivity, 95% specificity
29255892.study_design: retrospective case-control study with independent replication cohort

28149925.clinical_problem: detecting coarctation of the aorta in neonates from echocardiography
28149925.patient_population: 26 neonates with coarctation of the aorta and 64 normal neonates (validation set)
28149925.model_description: Two-dimensional echocardiogram clips from the parasternal long-axis, apical four-chamber and suprasternal notch views are classified by deep-learning-based classifiers per view; the combined decisions across the three standard views output a coarctation-of-the-aorta detection.
28149925.headline_result: total error rate 12.9% (11.5% false-negative, 13.6% false-positive) combining three standard echocardiographic views

28759710.exclusion_reason: resting-state fMRI ICA network analysis, no AI/ML diagnostic model

26120074.exclusion_reason: narrative review of fMRI error-processing findings, no AI/ML

26640765.clinical_problem: surveying multivariate/machine-learning analysis of fetal, neonatal and pediatric brain MRI for neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, ADHD, epilepsy, schizophrenia, and others)
26640765.patient_population: fetal, neonatal and pediatric patients undergoing brain MRI in the reviewed studies
26640765.model_description: Systematic review of multivariate analysis (statistical and machine learning pattern-recognition methods) applied to fetal, neonatal and pediatric brain MRI, covering diagnostic classification, disorder characterization and treatment monitoring across a range of neurodevelopmental disorders; no single model is developed.

39133401.model_family: multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus)
39133401.clinical_problem: interpreting pediatric radiological images and providing a diagnostic impression
39133401.patient_population: 30 medically significant pediatric radiology cases (90 images total)
39133401.model_description: Thirty pediatric radiology cases (90 images) with a short clinical history are submitted to three multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus), which generate a diagnostic impression; responses are independently scored for accuracy by a resident and an attending physician.
39133401.release_evidence: GPT-4 (OpenAI), Gemini 1.5 Pro (Google) and Claude 3 Opus (Anthropic) are named commercial vendor products
39133401.headline_result: correctly diagnosed 27.8% of images (25/90), partially correct 13.3%, incorrect 58.9%
39133401.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy evaluation of general-purpose multimodal LLMs

39389958.exclusion_reason: clinical disease review; AI mentioned only in passing as future direction

36455084.model_family: 2D+t convolutional neural network with transfer learning
36455084.clinical_problem: automatically describing anatomy and modeling operator workflow from first-trimester obstetric ultrasound scans
36455084.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing first-trimester obstetric ultrasound scanning
36455084.model_description: Full-length first-trimester ultrasound scan videos are analyzed by a 2D+t (spatio-temporal) convolutional neural network with transfer learning that automatically partitions the video into semantically meaningful segments based on detected fetal anatomy, enabling analysis of operator clinical workflow, skill, and time spent on key tasks such as nuchal translucency measurement.
36455084.dataset_size: 250 unlabeled video scans analyzed; additional labeled training data not quantified in abstract
36455084.headline_result: cross-validation accuracy 96.10%, F1=0.95, precision=0.94, recall=0.95; correlation with expert annotation ρ=0.95 (p=0.06)
36455084.study_design: retrospective technical development and workflow-analysis study

36910742.model_family: support vector machine on amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF)
36910742.clinical_problem: identifying adolescents with major depressive disorder and suicidal attempts using resting-state fMRI
36910742.patient_population: 71 first-episode, drug-naive adolescent MDD patients with suicidal attempts and 54 healthy controls
36910742.model_description: Resting-state fMRI amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) values in the bilateral medial superior frontal gyrus and precuneus are input to a support vector machine that classifies adolescents as having MDD with suicidal attempts or being healthy controls.
36910742.dataset_size: 71 adolescent MDD patients with suicidal attempts, 54 healthy controls
36910742.headline_result: SVM diagnostic accuracy 76.8% (medial superior frontal gyrus) and 82.4% (precuneus)
36910742.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

36952442.model_family: domain-guided (context-preserving cut-paste) data augmentation for deep neural networks
36952442.clinical_problem: benchmarking domain-specific data augmentation for a fetal ultrasound view-classification task
36952442.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images from the FETAL-125 and OB-125 benchmark datasets
36952442.model_description: Fetal ultrasound images undergo a domain-specific, context-preserving cut-paste augmentation strategy before training a neural network for view classification (standard fetal anatomical planes); performance with this augmentation is compared to traditional augmentation on the FETAL-125 and OB-125 benchmark datasets.
36952442.release_evidence: we provide open-source code to facilitate running bespoke data augmentations in an online fashion
36952442.study_design: retrospective technical benchmark study using public datasets

37857681.model_family: deep segmentation network with machine learning biometry pipeline
37857681.clinical_problem: automating linear biometric measurements of the fetal brain on MRI
37857681.patient_population: 268 MRI volumes (5,360 images) from normal fetuses
37857681.model_description: Fetal brain MRI is segmented by a deep network into cerebrum, cerebellum, and left/right lateral ventricles; the measurement plane is then automatically determined and biometric parameters (biparietal diameter, transverse cerebellar diameter, atrial diameters) are calculated per clinical guidelines and compared to manual measurements.
37857681.headline_result: correlation coefficients: CBPD 0.977, TCD 0.990, LAD 0.817, RAD 0.719
37857681.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and agreement study

37957363.clinical_problem: predicting brain age from cortical morphology to assess neurodevelopmental trajectory in preterm neonates
37957363.patient_population: 577 T1 MRI scans of preterm neonates from two datasets
37957363.model_description: Cortical surfaces and morphological features generated by the NEOCIVET pipeline from T1 MRI of preterm neonates are input to a graph convolutional network that predicts brain age; the difference between predicted and chronological age (brain age index) is related to perinatal risk factors and neurodevelopmental outcome at 30 months.
37957363.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.96 weeks, outperforming conventional machine learning methods without topological information

38157540.model_family: radiomics machine learning pipeline (FeAture Explorer / PyRadiomics) with logistic regression
38157540.clinical_problem: differentiating H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma from IDH-wild-type glioblastoma in adolescents and young adults
38157540.patient_population: 23 patients with G34m-DHG (mean age 23.7 years, range 11-45) and 30 patients with IDH-WT-GBM (mean age 30.96 years, range 5-43)
38157540.model_description: Conventional MRI features (VASARI) and radiomics features extracted with PyRadiomics are used to build a logistic regression / machine-learning pipeline (FeAture Explorer) that differentiates H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma from IDH-wild-type glioblastoma.
38157540.headline_result: radiomics-based model AUC 0.925 vs. VASARI-feature model AUC 0.843

34984672.model_family: support vector machine on functional connectivity
34984672.clinical_problem: distinguishing focal epilepsy patients from controls and lateralizing seizure onset using resting-state functional connectivity
34984672.patient_population: 103 adult and 65 pediatric focal epilepsy patients and 109 controls across four epilepsy centers
34984672.model_description: Resting-state fMRI whole-brain functional connectivity measures (parcelwise connectivity matrix, mean FC, degree of FC) are input to support vector machine models that classify epilepsy patients versus controls and lateralize the hemisphere of seizure onset, evaluated across four epilepsy centers.
34984672.dataset_size: 103 adult and 65 pediatric epilepsy patients, 109 controls (four centers)
34984672.headline_result: epilepsy-vs-control classification median accuracy 75.6% (AUC 0.83); lateralization median accuracy 64.0% (AUC 0.69)
34984672.study_design: retrospective multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study
